title: Heroku Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Alternatives
summary: Heroku pricing spans Standard to Enterprise tiers. You'll determine which tier covers your team's compute and database needs without overspending.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Does Heroku still have a free plan?


No. Heroku **retired its free dynos and free data tiers** in late 2022. As of November 2026 the cheapest way to run an app is the entry-level Eco dyno on a paid basis.


That means even a hobby project carries a recurring charge before you add a database. Budget for the dyno and the data store together, because the second line is the one people forget.


### How do I stop paying for an idle Heroku app?


Scale the dynos to zero, then remove or downgrade the add-ons, because add-ons keep billing whether or not any code runs. A stopped web process saves the dyno charge only. **A Postgres database attached to that app still accrues its full tier price every month.**


If you want the app back later, do these in order:


1. Take a backup.
2. Delete the database.
3. Restore it when you return.


If you only pause the dynos, you're paying for a database nobody is querying.


### Is Heroku Postgres billed separately from dynos?


Yes. Heroku Postgres is an add-on with its own tier and its own monthly price, and it appears as a separate line on the invoice. Changing dyno size does nothing to it.


For most production apps the database tier is the larger of the two lines, so compare plans on the dyno plus the database, not the dyno alone.


The same applies to every other add-on, such as caching, logging, or scheduling: each is metered on its own plan.


### Can I cap my Heroku bill?


Not with a hard stop that I can confirm as of this writing. What you can do is control the ceiling by controlling what you provision.


Dynos and add-ons are billed at fixed rates for the time they exist, so your worst case is the sum of the dyno count, dyno types, and add-on tiers you have switched on.


Avoid autoscaling rules you haven't tested, keep the maximum dyno count low, and review the usage page in the dashboard before the invoice closes. Check Heroku's current billing documentation for any spending alerts on your account type.


### Do I pay for Review apps?


Yes, for whatever they spin up. A Review app is a temporary copy of your app built for a pull request, and it uses dynos and any add-ons defined in its configuration.


Because billing is prorated for the time it runs, a short-lived review app is cheap and a forgotten one is not.


The practical fix is to keep review apps on the smallest dyno type, avoid giving each one a paid database tier, and let them be deleted automatically when the pull request closes.
